outcome:
Build "Service Request Tracker — Production Acceptance v0.2": a Node.js CLI app.

Capabilities (each MUST be implemented and verified):
1. Create: "node src/index.js create \"<title>\" \"<description>\"" writes a new request with status="open" and a generated id, then prints the id to stdout.
2. List: "node src/index.js list" prints all requests as a JSON array to stdout.
3. Update: "node src/index.js update <id> <new-status>" transitions status; valid forward transitions: open→in_progress, in_progress→resolved only. Reject same-status, backward, and unknown statuses.
4. Persist: store all requests in "data/requests.json" (create dir + file if absent).
5. Reject invalid inputs: empty title, unknown id, unknown new-status, invalid transition — each prints a clear error to stderr and exits code 1.
6. Automated tests using node:test (built-in): at least 6 cases covering (a) create, (b) list, (c) update, (d) persistence across restart, (e) invalid-input rejection, (f) one negative test.
7. README.md with: app description, install, run tests, CLI usage examples (create/list/update), valid status transitions table.

After producing all 5 files, finish with artifacts: ["package.json","README.md","src/index.js","src/store.js","test/app.test.js"].

After producing all files, npm test MUST exit 0 within 60 seconds.
context:
G7-19H — Live Production Acceptance. Real Z.ai + real OpenBot. Greenfield mission — NO missionInputs staged. The workers must design and produce the entire Service Request Tracker v0.2 from scratch using only Node.js >= 20 standard library (no external dependencies, no HTTP server, no browser).

REQUIRED FILE STRUCTURE (write ALL 5 files via write_file, then finish):
1. package.json — fields: name="service-request-tracker", version="0.2.0", type="module", scripts.test="node --test test/", scripts.start="node src/index.js". NO dependencies field (or empty). NO devDependencies.
2. README.md — sections: # Service Request Tracker, ## What it does, ## Install (npm install — no deps), ## Run tests (npm test), ## CLI usage (create/list/update examples), ## Valid status transitions (open→in_progress→resolved, forward-only).
3. src/store.js — exported functions: loadRequests() reads data/requests.json (returns [] if absent, creates dir + file if missing); saveRequests(arr) writes data/requests.json atomically; createRequest(title, description) returns a new {id,title,description,status:"open",createdAt} and persists it; listRequests() returns the array; updateStatus(id, newStatus) — validates id exists, validates new-status is known value, validates forward-only transition, throws on invalid input.
4. src/index.js — CLI entrypoint: parses process.argv, dispatches to src/store.js functions. Exit codes: 0 on success, 1 on user input error, 2 on internal error.
5. test/app.test.js — uses node:test + node:assert. At least 6 tests covering (a) create, (b) list, (c) update, (d) persistence across restart, (e) invalid-input rejection, (f) one negative test.

STATUS TRANSITIONS:
- open → in_progress (allowed)
- in_progress → resolved (allowed)
- open → resolved (FORBIDDEN — must go through in_progress first; throw)
- Any backward (resolved → in_progress, etc.) — REJECT (throw)
- Same-status (open → open) — REJECT (throw)
- Unknown new-status string — REJECT (throw)

ACCEPTANCE: write_file 5 times (one per file), then finish with the 5 artifact paths. NO external dependencies. NO new files beyond the 5 listed. NO test framework other than node:test.

CLEAN ROOM GUARANTEE: after the mission, an independent clean-room run will: (1) cd into the produced package, (2) npm install (must be a no-op), (3) npm test (must exit 0 within 60s), (4) run the CLI: create, list, update, list — verifying CRUD + persistence + invalid-input rejection.
